The PGA TOUR heads to Kentucky this week for the ISCO Championship. The tournament will be contested at a new home for 2025, as the Hurstbourne Country Club in Louisville, Kentucky. This marks the fourth year in a row that the event allows access to 50 DP World Tour members. Newly minted pro Gordon Sargent is set to tee it up at the ISCO Championship after finding the weekend in two straight TOUR starts. Sargent, who earned his TOUR card via PGA TOUR University Accelerated, is averaging over 329 yards per pop off the tee so far in his young career – which would rank him No. 1 on TOUR. Emiliano Grillo is back in action at the ISCO Championship after a runner-up finish at the John Deere Classic for his first top-10 finish on TOUR since last March. Joining these two is a hoard of young talent, including: Rico Hoey, Michael Thorbjornsen, Kevin Roy, Angel Ayora and the game’s top-ranked male amateur golfer, Jackson Koivun, from the University of Auburn.
